summary: RELEASED COVER REFERENCE. The published Issue 1 cover is canonical and should not be regenerated or replaced unless explicitly reopened. Its production role here is to document the series cover language: premium luminous marine-park spectacle, Maya as the human anchor, strong white AZURE REACH masthead, cyan wave accent, Star Splitter Visions mark at upper left, and a compact issue-number block at upper right.
settingText: Azure Reach public atrium/open-ocean presentation space: luminous blue aquarium glass, sweeping luxury architecture, reflective surfaces and abundant marine life.
panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PORTRAIT COVER; no interior panel grid. The actual released Issue 1 cover pixels are the authority. Do not reinterpret this recipe as permission to redesign the published cover.

Brand read: very large white AZURE REACH masthead across the upper quarter with the established angular A/wave treatment, deep navy field and cyan accent; Star Splitter Visions mark upper left; narrow issue-number block upper right.

Illustration read: Maya is the dominant central human silhouette, confident and work-ready rather than superheroic, surrounded by the polished public park and supporting ensemble. A large marine animal crosses the luminous upper-right water field so wonder and workplace coexist in one image.
Thumbnail read: the giant white masthead, Maya's dark central silhouette, and saturated blue aquarium field must remain legible when reduced.
This cover is a released brand anchor, not the compositional template for later issues.

directionInline.text: COVER AUTHORITY — Released StarSplitterVisions asset sites/visions/public/images/covers/azure-reach-issue-01-cover.jpg is canonical. Retrieve and inspect its actual pixels before any Azure Reach cover production session. Never replace it from prose alone.

TRADE-DRESS SCOPE — This released cover controls masthead geometry, publisher-mark placement, issue-number block, cyan/white/navy title hierarchy, polish level and overall brand confidence. It does NOT require later covers to repeat the ensemble lineup, Maya-centered composition, promotional callouts or exact illustration palette.
NO EXTRA TEXT — Do not invent environmental signage, blurbs, handles, credits or promotional copy beyond exact scripted cover lettering.

source: Released StarSplitterVisions Issue 1 cover; encoded as cover-production authority.

summary: Sell the issue by making the dolphin impossible to look away from, then letting one tiny returned phone create the human story. The animal and the luminous Dolphin Gallery are the primary attraction; the misunderstanding is the second read. Julian and Pip may register the public reaction, but no human figure should compete with the dolphin. Do not reveal the later controlled demonstration, training-object explanation, souvenir solution or retail handoff.
settingText: Dolphin Gallery at the public glass: luminous blue habitat, dry-side keeper return ledge, elegant barrier and a cluster of guests close enough to feel personally chosen without crossing any boundary.
panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PORTRAIT COVER. FIRST READ: a magnificent dolphin sweeping close through luminous cobalt water, large enough to dominate the lower two-thirds of the illustration. The animal's body, movement, reflected light and scale must be beautiful enough to sell Azure Reach even if the reader notices nothing else.

SECOND READ: at the dry-side keeper return point near the glass, an intact smartphone has just been nudged or deposited into the return area. It is a small but unmistakable anomaly inside the beautiful image—not the largest object on the page.

A few guests beyond the glass are transfixed. One looks from the returned phone to an object in their own hand. Their reaction should make the contagious interpretation understandable without depicting anyone actually dropping another object.
Julian and Pip may appear as secondary public-side figures noticing the same shift. Keep them small enough that the dolphin remains the cover star.
Composition hierarchy: DOLPHIN -> LUMINOUS HABITAT -> RETURNED PHONE -> HUMAN REACTION. Do not invert that order.
The dolphin is natural, powerful and behaviorally credible. No smile, wink, presenting gesture or sentimental eye contact that assigns human intention.
Reserve the upper 27–30% for the established AZURE REACH masthead/trade dress, using clean deep-blue water and light shafts as the negative-space field.
Thumbnail test: at small size the cover must first read as a spectacular dolphin image; on a second glance the phone and human reaction must still be discoverable.
Spoiler ceiling: no blue training tokens, formal Retrieval Window demonstration, branded souvenir, behavior card, completion-point retail, later public correction or final solution.

directionInline.text: COVER PURPOSE — Wonder is the sale; the misunderstanding is the hook. The reader should want to be at the Dolphin Gallery before wondering whether the dolphin 'gave' the phone back.

PIXEL-READ TRADE DRESS — Before generation, retrieve and inspect the actual released Issue 1 cover pixels. Match masthead geometry, publisher-mark position, issue-number architecture and premium finish only; do not copy its ensemble-poster composition or promotional blurbs.
ANIMAL RULE — The dolphin is never the joke and never performs a human emotion for the cover. Human interpretation creates the comedy.
NO EXTRA TEXT — No social-media comments, environmental slogans, fake headlines, labels or additional promotional copy.

source: Azure Reach season cover pass, September 30 2026.

summary: Sell the tidepool itself first: a jewel-like living world at human scale that makes proximity feel genuinely valuable. The premium-access tension is a second-read human detail at the edge of that beauty. Pip carries the boundary without becoming the visual star. Do not reveal the microscope discovery, improved photography, rope removal, expert-access solution or final premium model.
settingText: Bright jewel-like Tidepool Gallery: shallow living pools, wet-edge boundary, polished stone and stainless detailing, with a discreet premium-group presence inside a still-public habitat.
panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PORTRAIT COVER. FIRST READ: an immersive near-water/macro tidepool image—jewel-toned anemones, sea stars, urchins, tiny crabs, textured rock, clear rippling water and reflected cyan light. The living tidepool should occupy most of the page and be beautiful enough to make the reader want to lean closer.

Use an almost-at-water-level perspective rather than a detached overhead diagram. Give the organisms credible scale, texture and biological specificity; the cover should feel sensuous, intimate and alive.
SECOND READ: a tasteful premium wristband/lanyard and a guest hand hover at the wet-edge boundary while Pip, smaller in frame, quietly controls the space. The hand never touches an animal.
Julian may be omitted unless the composition genuinely benefits from a small public-facing figure. Do not add extra cast simply to represent the ensemble.
Composition hierarchy: LIVING TIDEPOOL -> HUMAN DESIRE FOR PROXIMITY -> PIP'S BOUNDARY -> VIP STATUS DETAIL.
Use a restrained champagne/gold premium accent against Azure Reach cyan/aquamarine, but never let VIP graphics become more visually attractive than the habitat.
Reserve the upper 27–30% for the established masthead using water reflection, pale stone or controlled dark architecture as clean negative space.
Thumbnail test: the cover must first read as an extraordinary tidepool image; the reaching hand/wristband and Pip become the curiosity on the second read.
Spoiler ceiling: no microscope projection, expert-led interpretation as the answer, improved overhead photo, removed rope, adoption discussion, sponsor approval or resolved premium format.

directionInline.text: COVER PURPOSE — Make the reader want the experience before asking what VIP can actually buy. If the habitat is not the most desirable element on the cover, the composition has failed.
PIXEL-READ TRADE DRESS — Inspect the released Issue 1 cover pixels before generation and inherit only masthead, publisher mark, issue-number block and polished brand rhythm.
CHARACTER RULE — Pip is competent and warm, not a bouncer; the premium guest is sincerely excited, not entitled or villainous.
ANIMAL RULE — No touching, handling, distress, crowding or staged animal performance.
NO EXTRA TEXT — No invented VIP signage, slogans, social posts, price tags or promotional copy.

source: Azure Reach season cover pass, September 30 2026.

summary: Sell the ray habitat as one of Azure Reach's most breathtaking experiences. A huge ray in luminous motion is the cover's primary subject; only after that should the reader notice that the expensive live camera is framing the wrong part of the spectacle. The cover promises beauty first and the broadcast problem second. Do not reveal the later feeding arrival, expert-question format, staff-camera mistake or successful final stream.
settingText: Ray Gallery during a scheduled livestream: luminous deep-blue habitat, one premium public-side camera position, clean feeding zone, polished glass and viewers gathering behind the production footprint.
panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PORTRAIT COVER. FIRST READ: one magnificent ray dominates the page, sweeping diagonally through deep luminous blue water with wings catching shafts of light; a second ray or distant silhouettes may add depth. The animal should feel huge, graceful and worth watching independent of the story problem.
Let particulate water, feeding-zone depth, glass reflections and habitat scale create a cinematic marine image. This must never read as an empty-tank cover.

SECOND READ: low at one edge of the composition, a professional livestream camera and its small monitor/viewfinder are aimed at a technically correct but visually inadequate slice of the habitat—empty feeding-zone water or merely the trailing edge of the animal we can see magnificently outside the in-world frame.

Julian and Kyler can be small figures beside the rig, both aware that the real spectacle is happening somewhere the camera is not effectively presenting. Their expressions should be restrained; the situation is the joke.

The reader's comic-book viewpoint is intentionally better than the in-world camera viewpoint. Do not let diegetic broadcast failure deprive the reader of the animal wonder the broadcast is trying to capture.
Composition hierarchy: RAY -> VAST BLUE HABITAT -> TINY CAMERA/VIEWFINDER MISMATCH -> HUMAN REACTION.
Reserve the upper 27–30% for the established masthead against clean deep cobalt water. One tiny red tally-light accent is enough to signal live production.
Thumbnail test: first read must be BIG BEAUTIFUL RAY. Second read reveals the little camera aiming at the wrong place.
Spoiler ceiling: no successful feeding-frame payoff, revised sponsor graphics, expert-Q&A solution, accidental staff feed, final no-countdown format or later stream resolution.

directionInline.text: COVER PURPOSE — The animal spectacle is what makes the production problem worth caring about. Never center empty water, the monitor, or the camera over the ray.
PIXEL-READ TRADE DRESS — Inspect the released Issue 1 cover pixels and match its cover branding only; do not borrow its ensemble-poster staging.
ANIMAL RULE — Rays are safe, natural, majestic and not 'late.' The camera is wrong for the moment; the animals are not.
NO EXTRA TEXT — Avoid fake livestream comments, sponsor copy, UI clutter or environmental signage. Let the tiny red tally light carry 'live' visually.

source: Azure Reach season cover pass, September 30 2026.

summary: Sell Conservation Week through the thing the campaign is supposed to make people care about: a spectacular living experience. The towering schooling-fish habitat and the returning Turtle-Helmet Kid carry the cover; the campaign passport is the small second-read complication pulling his attention away. Nia witnesses the contradiction rather than dominating it. Do not reveal the later abandoned passport, campaign redesign, audited total or sponsor resolution.
settingText: Azure Reach's towering schooling-fish cylinder / open-ocean public space during Conservation Week: immense turning fish above the public floor, campaign passport materials present only as a small human-scale layer.
panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PORTRAIT COVER. FIRST READ: an immense turning school of fish fills most of the vertical page, silver-blue bodies catching light in a coordinated living vortex above a tiny child. The habitat must be breathtaking enough that the reader understands why somebody could forget the campaign entirely.
Turtle-Helmet Kid stands small beneath the school, visibly caught by the sight. The scale contrast—tiny child, enormous living movement—is the emotional center.

SECOND READ: the Conservation Week passport in the Kid's hand or foreground carries several bright activity icons/stamp targets, tugging his attention toward the next task. Do not show it abandoned; he is still actively participating at this point.
Nia may appear small at the edge of the public space, observing the difference between the child's reaction to the fish and his reaction to the campaign card. She is not posed as the answer.
Campaign graphics should be polished and appealing but physically small beside the living habitat. Never let a dashboard, counter or Conservation Wall become the most beautiful object on the cover.
Composition hierarchy: SCHOOLING FISH / LIVING SCALE -> CHILD'S AWE -> PASSPORT OBJECTIVE -> NIA'S OBSERVATION.
Reserve the upper 27–30% for the established masthead using deep open-ocean blue and the upper arc of the school as a clean branded field.
Thumbnail test: first read is a spectacular vertical school of fish with one tiny child beneath it. The passport becomes discoverable only after the wonder has already landed.

Spoiler ceiling: do not show the passport forgotten on a bench, the mangrove preference payoff, deduplicated count, redesigned campaign, deleted fifty-thousand headline, sponsor acceptance or Anniversary Gala setup.

directionInline.text: COVER PURPOSE — The conservation subject, not the measurement apparatus, is the sale. The reader should care about the living park before noticing how the campaign may be redirecting attention.
PIXEL-READ TRADE DRESS — Inspect the released Issue 1 cover pixels and preserve the established masthead, publisher mark, issue-number block and premium finish only.
GUEST RULE — Turtle-Helmet Kid is genuinely delighted by both discovery and completion games; do not turn him into a symbolic scold or make the campaign look obviously foolish.
NO EXTRA TEXT — No exact engagement totals, slogans, dashboards, fake hashtags or promotional copy beyond the scripted trade dress.

source: Azure Reach season cover pass, September 30 2026.

summary: Sell the finale as the most beautiful night Azure Reach can stage: an overwhelming living reef and elegant anniversary gala layered together so successfully that the reader wants to attend. Only on the second read should the abundance begin to look competitive. Beatrice is the human focal owner, but the park itself remains the star. Do not reveal which elements are later cut, combined, protected or refused.
settingText: Coral Grand Hall and connected anniversary-gala public space at night: enormous luminous reef, thousands of small fish, reflective stone and glass, elegant guests and restrained champagne-gold event details.
panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PORTRAIT COVER. FIRST READ: Azure Reach at its most spectacular—an enormous living reef or sweeping school fills the vertical background with saturated blue light, coral architecture and depth; elegantly dressed guests become small against the habitat.

Beatrice is the strongest human figure but not larger than the experience. Place her in the lower foreground or midground with a gala program/event map, looking up at the room she helped create rather than posing toward the reader.

Layer beautiful gala elements around the edges—restrained projection, florals, small-plate hospitality, donor seating, camera position, polished evening dress. Every individual element should look desirable.
SECOND READ: the gala elements are beginning to compete for the same sightlines and floor space. Let that pressure emerge from overlap and abundance, not clutter or disaster staging.
Maya may appear deeper on the open habitat axis as a small visual counterweight. Julian can be omitted unless needed for one additional public-facing layer.
Composition hierarchy: LIVING REEF / PARK SCALE -> GALA BEAUTY -> BEATRICE -> TOO-MANY-GOOD-THINGS PRESSURE.
This is the season's richest cover, but the habitat must remain more visually magnetic than sponsor architecture, event graphics or human staging.
Reserve the upper 27–30% for the established masthead against deep navy/cobalt water. Use restrained champagne-gold accents without turning the environment into a dark ballroom.
Thumbnail test: first read is unmistakably a spectacular Azure Reach reef-at-night image. Beatrice and the gala richness appear as the second layer, not the other way around.

Spoiler ceiling: do not show the simplified final program, removed sponsor wall, protected care windows, reduced rehearsal, ray refusal, stream recovery, award interruption payoff, board expansion request or final resolution.

directionInline.text: COVER PURPOSE — The reader should want an invitation to this gala before noticing why the program may need to get out of the park's way.

PIXEL-READ TRADE DRESS — Inspect the released Issue 1 cover pixels and preserve its masthead architecture, publisher mark, issue-number treatment and premium marine-park finish. Do not copy its cast-lineup composition.
TONE RULE — Prestige workplace comedy through abundance, not disaster. No distressed animals, emergency lighting, villain framing or ugly event design.
NO EXTRA TEXT — No sponsor names, gala slogans, fake schedules, signage, credits or promotional copy beyond the scripted cover trade dress.

source: Azure Reach season cover pass, September 30 2026.
